plan: Since this is effectively a second-price auction (the ascending clock mechanism means I pay the second-highest bid if I win), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the competitors' bids, and I pay only the second-highest bid, which is always profitable or break-even. Bidding higher risks overpaying; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Thus, I will bid exactly $36, my true value, to maximize expected profit.

Since this is essentially a second-price auction (the ascending clock ends when the second-highest sealed bid is reached, and the winner pays that price), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities where the second-highest bid is between my true value and my bid. Bidding my value of $33 ensures I maximize expected profit regardless of others' bids.

Since the auction functions as a second-price auction (the winner pays the second-highest bid/exit price), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win, while bidding lower risks losing an auction I could have profitably won. With a value of $31, bidding exactly $31 ensures I maximize expected profit: I win whenever the highest competing bid is below $31, paying only that competing bid, and I never overpay.
